text:
markdown-docx 0.3.7 syntax

Supported Markdown:
  ATX headings, paragraphs, emphasis, strong text, inline code, hard line breaks, fenced code blocks, blockquotes, ordered and unordered lists, pipe tables, links, and images.

Links use [link text](https://example.com) and become native Word hyperlinks. Labels preserve inline formatting and optional titles become tooltips. Reference links, angle-bracket autolinks, mailto links, relative file links, and linked inline images are supported wherever their content is allowed. Relative file links resolve from the output document. Destinations are not fetched. Bare URLs remain plain text. Every heading creates a bookmark. Link to its slug with `[Details](#details)`, including before the heading. Slugs use plain heading text and image labels, normalized to NFC and lowercase. Punctuation is removed except underscores and hyphens. Whitespace becomes a hyphen. Empty slugs use `section`. Duplicates receive `-1`, `-2`, and later available suffixes in document order. Unicode and percent-encoded fragments are supported. Fragments must match the slug exactly. Missing targets produce `internal_link_unresolved` with the source line. Word bookmark names are generated separately to fit Word constraints.

Lists: the first ordered marker sets the starting number, including zero. Later markers do not reset numbering. Separate lists restart independently. Nested lists have independent sequences. Indented continuation paragraphs are unnumbered and aligned with item text. Mapped list styles must reference native template numbering.

Footnotes use the named `[^label]` and `[^label]: note text` extension from mdit-py-plugins. Labels are case-sensitive. Forward references, formatted text, links, hard breaks, and multiple note paragraphs are supported. Indent later paragraphs by four spaces. Each label must be defined and referenced exactly once. Empty notes are allowed. Undefined labels, duplicate definitions, unused definitions, and repeated references produce line-aware errors. Notes cannot contain images, lists, tables, headings, code blocks, metadata, or nested notes. References in image labels are rejected. References render as native Word notes with automatic numbering. No custom directive is required.

Pipe-table header rows repeat automatically when a table spans pages in Word. Body rows are not marked as headers. No Markdown directive is required. The underlying library exposes `row.repeat_as_header` for callers that need explicit control.

Images: alt text becomes the Word image description. Optional Markdown image titles become image titles. Standalone, inline, and linked images support both. Formatting markers in alt text are removed while their text is preserved. Empty descriptions stay empty without marking images as decorative.

Metadata comments:
  document metadata must be first
  section metadata starts a next-page section
  <!-- markdown-docx: page-break --> inserts a page break
  table metadata must immediately precede a pipe table
  image metadata must immediately precede a standalone image

Fonts: document.fonts.body and document.fonts.headings set Latin theme fonts. Mapped styles inherit from those theme slots. Omitted overrides preserve template settings. document.fonts.monospace stays explicit for code. Fonts are not embedded or installed.

Lengths use in, cm, mm, or pt. Image widths may also use percentages.

Unsupported in 0.3.7:
  empty link destinations, raw HTML, task lists, horizontal rules, indented code blocks, DOTX, floating images, headers and footers from Markdown, page-number fields, and direct OOXML features.

fonts.body: nonempty font name for the minor Latin theme font
fonts.headings: nonempty font name for the major Latin theme font
fonts.monospace: nonempty fixed font name for code, default Consolas
